image_description: Two male ducks (drakes) swimming in rippled water. The duck on the right is a Northern Pintail or similar species with a dark brown head, white breast, and grey body, featuring a long, slender neck and pointed tail. The duck on the left is partially visible, showing a dark green iridescent head and grey body, resembling a Mallard. Both are floating naturally on the water surface.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bills visible are not the typical broad, flat mallard-style bill. The right duck has a slender, pointed black bill (characteristic of Pintails/Shovelers), and the left duck has a yellowish but relatively slender bill. They do not match the 'broad, flat' description strictly, though they are valid duck bills.
Both visible heads show small, dark eyes consistent with avian anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Both subjects exhibit streamlined, buoyant bodies floating correctly on the water line. Plumage appears dense and waterproof.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The left duck shows the classic iridescent green head of a Mallard. The right duck shows a dark brown/chestnut head with white breast, fitting the 'chestnut head' variant description or a different drake species (Pintail).

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The legs and feet are submerged beneath the water surface and are completely occluded. Cannot verify webbing or leg placement.
The folded wings on the back of both ducks appear structurally sound, broad, and tapered at the ends, consistent with resting waterfowl anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The duck on the right clearly displays elongated, pointed central tail feathers (characteristic of Northern Pintail drakes). The left duck's tail is less distinct but appears short and upturned.
